# ferriskey_client_scope_protocol_mapper (Resource)

Manages a protocol mapper attached to a client scope. The API has no single-mapper read endpoint, so the mapper is read through its parent client scope.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ferriskey_client_scope_protocol_mapper" "email_claim" {
  realm       = ferriskey_realm.acme.name
  scope_id    = ferriskey_client_scope.billing.scope_id
  name        = "email-claim"
  mapper_type = "oidc-usermodel-attribute-mapper"

  config = {
    "claim.name"         = "email"
    "user.attribute"     = "email"
    "id.token.claim"     = "true"
    "access.token.claim" = "true"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `mapper_type` (String) Mapper implementation type, e.g. `oidc-usermodel-attribute-mapper` or `oidc-audience-mapper`.
- `name` (String) Mapper name.
- `realm` (String) Name of the realm the scope belongs to. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `scope_id` (String) UUID of the client scope that owns the mapper. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `config` (Map of String) Mapper configuration as string key/value pairs, e.g. `claim.name`, `user.attribute`, `id.token.claim`. Only the keys you specify are tracked; changing it replaces the stored configuration.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Composite identifier `{realm}/{scope_id}/{mapper_id}`.
- `mapper_id` (String) Server-assigned UUID of the protocol mapper.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import ferriskey_client_scope_protocol_mapper.email_claim acme/4b2d7f90-1111-2222-3333-444455556666/9c1e0a33-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-ddddeeeeffff
```
